footer.note: Data from issuers' official holdings files and SEC N-PORT; falls back to the Yahoo Finance top 10 (flagged) when full holdings are unavailable.

items.a: Overlap measures how similar two ETFs are: for every stock both funds hold, take the smaller of the two weights and add them up. The higher the number, the more you are buying the same stocks twice.
Owning several ETFs looks diversified, but if their top holdings coincide (for example VOO and IVV both track the S&P 500), your risk is still concentrated in the same companies.

items.q: Where does the data come from, and is it accurate?
items.a: Issuers' official daily holdings files (iShares, Vanguard, SPDR, Invesco) first; then SEC N-PORT filings (quarterly, so they can lag by months); only if neither is available does the tool fall back to the Yahoo Finance top 10, and it flags that clearly.
